title: Longitudinal ICU phenotype clustering
summary: Candidate coordinates for data-driven longitudinal phenotypes. Cohort construction, feature scaling, missingness, distance or model choice, cluster-number selection, stability, and external reproducibility must be separated from downstream outcome association.

design_candidates.population: A reproducibly defined ICU cohort with enough repeated measurements in a common observation window.
design_candidates.time_zero: A shared clinical landmark such as ICU admission or syndrome onset, before trajectory extraction.
design_candidates.observation_window: A fixed longitudinal window and grid with explicit aggregation, missingness, and survivor-selection handling.
design_candidates.prediction_or_followup_window: Outcome comparisons begin after phenotype assignment unless outcomes are strictly descriptive labels.
eligibility_candidates: Avoid selecting clusters by outcome separation
design_candidates.exposure: Unsupervised phenotype assignment derived only from prespecified longitudinal features.
design_candidates.outcome: Cluster stability, reproducibility, and secondary clinical outcomes not used to choose the clustering solution.
design_candidates.estimand: Descriptive phenotype structure and, secondarily, adjusted outcome contrasts across stable assignments.
recommended_methods: Multiple internal validity and stability criteria

stop_conditions: Repeated measurements cannot be aligned to a common landmark
Cluster number is selected solely by outcome association
No stability assessment can be performed

citations.title: Temporal trends in sepsis phenotypes and clinical outcomes
